data.description: The Memorandum of Association (MOA) of a company defines its fundamental objectives and the scope of its operations. Altering these objects is a significant corporate action that allows a company to adjust its activities in response to new market opportunities, strategic shifts, or regulatory changes. This process involves revising the MOA to reflect the updated objectives, which requires careful handling to ensure compliance with legal requirements and smooth execution.

eligibility.name: Eligibility

data.title: Board Approval

data.title: Shareholder Consent
data.description: The proposed change must be ratified by a special resolution passed by the shareholders in a general meeting. This ensures that the shareholders, who are the owners of the company, are informed and supportive of the new objectives.

data.title: Legal Compliance
data.description: The alteration must comply with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, and other relevant regulations. This includes adhering to procedural requirements and filing the necessary forms with the Registrar of Companies (ROC).

registration_process.name: Process
registration_process.heading: The process for altering the objects of a company involves several detailed steps

data.title: Board Meeting
data.description: Conduct a board meeting to discuss and approve the proposed change in objects. The board should draft and pass a resolution documenting their approval. This resolution must be recorded in the meeting minutes.

data.title: General Meeting
data.description: Call a general meeting of shareholders to pass a special resolution. Proper notice of the meeting must be sent to all shareholders, and the resolution must be passed by the required majority.

data.title: Filing Forms with ROC
data.description: Submit Form MGT-14 to file the special resolution with the ROC indicating shareholder approval, and Form INC-24 to obtain ROC approval for the alteration of the MOA.

data.title: Updating the MOA
data.description: Amend the Memorandum of Association to reflect the new or revised objectives. Ensure that the updated MOA is filed with the ROC for official recognition.

data.title: Notification
data.description: Inform stakeholders, including clients, suppliers, and financial institutions, about the change in the company's objectives to ensure continued business relations and compliance.

data.title: Public Disclosure

data.description: A change in the directors of a company is a significant event that requires adherence to legal provisions under the Companies Act, 2013. It can occur due to resignation of an existing director, appointment of an additional director, replacement due to retirement or death, disqualification of a director, or board expansion. The change involves updating official records and intimating the Registrar of Companies (ROC) to maintain transparency and compliance.

data.title: For Appointment as a Director
data.description: The individual must be at least 18 years of age and possess a Director Identification Number (DIN). There should be no disqualification as per Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013, including insolvency, conviction by a court, or failure to file financial statements for three years.

data.title: For Resignation as a Director
data.description: The director can submit a resignation letter to the board, and the company must intimate the ROC within 30 days. The outgoing director must ensure that the company has filed all necessary forms to avoid any future liabilities.

data.title: Fresh Expertise
data.description: New directors bring their industry expertise, leadership skills, and fresh ideas, driving innovation and growth.

data.title: Improved Corporate Governance
data.description: A diverse board ensures better decision-making and governance, enhancing the company's overall performance.

data.title: Business Expansion
data.description: Appointing directors with new market insights can drive growth strategies and open new business opportunities.

data.title: Removal of Ineffective Leadership
data.description: The resignation or removal of an underperforming director helps in maintaining a dynamic and efficient board.

data.title: Reduced Legal Liability

requirement.name: Information Required
requirement.heading: To ensure a smooth transition in the director's position, the following information is required

data.title: Director's Personal Details
data.description: Full name, address, contact information, Director Identification Number (DIN), PAN Card and Aadhaar Card for KYC purposes.

data.title: Director's Consent or Resignation Letter
data.description: Consent in Form DIR-2 for appointment of a new director, or resignation letter in case of an exiting director.

data.title: Board Resolution
data.description: A copy of the board resolution approving the appointment or resignation of the director.

data.title: Declaration by the Appointed Director
data.description: A declaration confirming that the new director is not disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013.

data.title: Resignation of a Director
data.description: The director submits a resignation letter to the Board. A board meeting is conducted to accept the resignation and pass a resolution. The company files Form DIR-12 with the ROC within 30 days along with the board resolution and resignation letter. Statutory registers including the Register of Directors are then updated.

data.title: Appointment of a New Director
data.description: The individual provides consent in Form DIR-2 to become a director. The company holds a board meeting to pass a resolution for the appointment and files Form DIR-12 with the ROC within 30 days. An appointment letter is issued and statutory registers are updated.

data.title: Replacement of a Retiring Director
data.description: In case of a retiring director, a resolution is passed during the AGM with shareholders' consent. If a new director is appointed in place of the retiring one, Form DIR-12 is filed with the ROC as per the standard appointment process.

compliances.name: Compliances
compliances.heading: After completing the process of changing directors, the company must adhere to several compliance obligations

data.title: ROC Filings
data.description: File Form DIR-12 within 30 days of appointment or resignation with the necessary attachments. Ensure all pending financial statements and annual returns are filed, especially if the outgoing director had liabilities.

data.title: Update Statutory Registers
data.description: The Register of Directors and Register of Key Managerial Personnel must be updated to reflect the changes.

data.title: Disclosure in Annual Return
data.description: Any changes in the directorship must be disclosed in the company's annual return (Form MGT-7).

data.title: Intimation to Stakeholders
data.description: The company may notify stakeholders, banks, and other financial institutions of the change in director, ensuring continuity in operations.

data.title: Compliance with Tax and Legal Authorities
data.description: Intimate the necessary tax authorities, banks, and other relevant parties to avoid any complications arising from the change.

data.title: What are the reasons for changing a director in a company?
data.description: A company may change its directors due to various reasons such as resignation, appointment of new directors, disqualification, retirement, or death of a director.

data.title: What is the process of appointing a new director in a company?
data.description: The process involves obtaining consent from the individual in Form DIR-2, conducting a board meeting to approve the appointment, and filing Form DIR-12 with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) within 30 days.

data.title: What is Form DIR-12, and when is it required?
data.description: Form DIR-12 is filed with the ROC to notify any changes in the company's board of directors, including appointments, resignations, or removals. It must be filed within 30 days of the board resolution.

data.title: Can a director resign voluntarily?
data.description: Yes, a director can resign by submitting a resignation letter to the board, which must then be accepted and filed with the ROC using Form DIR-12.

data.title: What are the eligibility criteria for becoming a director?
data.description: To be eligible, an individual must be at least 18 years old, possess a valid Director Identification Number (DIN), and not be disqualified under Section 164 of the Companies Act, 2013.

data.title: What documents are needed to change a director in a company?
data.description: Required documents include the director's resignation letter (if applicable), Form DIR-2 (for new appointment), board resolution, and Form DIR-12, along with the director's personal details such as DIN, PAN, and Aadhaar.

data.title: What happens if the company fails to file Form DIR-12 within the stipulated time?
data.description: Failure to file Form DIR-12 within the 30-day deadline can result in penalties and late fees imposed by the ROC.

data.title: Is it mandatory to update the statutory registers after changing a director?
data.description: Yes, companies must update their Register of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel after any change in directorship.

data.title: Can a director be removed without consent?
data.description: Yes, a director can be removed by passing a resolution in a general meeting if shareholders vote in favor of the removal, subject to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.

title: Change in Name of Company
description: A company may need to change its name for various strategic reasons including rebranding, merger or acquisition, or change in business focus. Changing a company's name involves a legal process governed by the Companies Act. We provide end-to-end assistance for a smooth and compliant name change process.

data.description: The name of a company is its identity in the business world. Sometimes companies may need to change this name for reasons such as rebranding, merger or acquisition, change in business focus, or other strategic reasons. However, changing a company's name is not just a matter of preference but involves a legal process governed by the provisions of the Companies Act. All communications, official documents, and registrations must be updated after the name change is approved by the Registrar of Companies.

eligibility.name: Eligibility
eligibility.heading: A company must meet the following eligibility criteria to initiate a name change

data.title: Registered Entity
data.description: The company must be a legally registered entity under the Companies Act.

data.title: Board and Shareholder Approval
data.description: The decision to change the name must be approved by the Board of Directors and the shareholders through a special resolution.

data.title: Authorized by Articles of Association (AOA)
data.description: The company's Articles of Association (AOA) must allow for the name change. If the AOA does not permit this, it must be amended before proceeding.

data.title: Rebranding and Market Positioning
data.description: Changing the name allows companies to rebrand and reposition themselves in the market, especially if their original name no longer reflects their business focus.

data.title: Business Expansion
data.description: A name change might be necessary when a company diversifies its services or products and the current name no longer aligns with the new offerings.

data.title: Mergers or Acquisitions
data.description: Companies undergoing mergers, acquisitions, or restructuring may need a new name to represent the newly formed entity.

data.title: Legal or Regulatory Requirements
data.description: A name change may be necessary to comply with trademark laws or to resolve disputes with other entities holding similar names.

data.title: Global Appeal
data.description: Companies expanding internationally might change their name to one that is more recognizable or acceptable globally.

requirement.name: Information Required
requirement.heading: To proceed with a name change, the company will need the following

data.title: Existing Company Name
data.description: The current legal name of the company.

data.title: Proposed New Name
data.description: At least three alternative names to be submitted for approval by the Registrar of Companies (ROC).

data.title: Articles of Association (AOA)
data.description: The company's AOA must either allow for a name change or be amended to include such provisions.

data.title: Board and Shareholder Resolutions
data.description: Resolutions passed by the board and the shareholders authorizing the name change.

data.title: Company Incorporation Certificate
data.description: A copy of the company's current certificate of incorporation.

data.title: Board Meeting
data.description: Convene a board meeting to discuss and approve the proposal for changing the company name. Pass a board resolution to authorize the directors to conduct an Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM) with shareholders.

data.title: Name Availability Check
data.description: Submit the proposed new names to the Registrar of Companies (ROC) for approval through Form RUN (Reserve Unique Name) to ensure the names are not already in use.

data.title: Extraordinary General Meeting (EGM)
data.description: Once the name availability is confirmed, send notices to shareholders to convene an EGM. Pass a special resolution approving the name change and any amendments to the company's Articles of Association.

data.title: Filing with the Registrar of Companies (ROC)
data.description: File Form MGT-14 with the ROC within 30 days along with the certified copy of the resolution. Then submit Form INC-24 to officially apply for the change in company name with required attachments.

data.title: Issuance of New Certificate of Incorporation
data.description: Once the ROC approves the name change, the company will receive a new Certificate of Incorporation reflecting the updated name.

data.title: Amending Legal Documents
data.description: Update the company's legal documents including contracts, agreements, and licenses to reflect the new name.

compliances.name: Compliances
compliances.heading: Once the company name is changed, several compliance actions need to be undertaken

data.title: Update Statutory Registers
data.description: The company's statutory registers, including the Register of Members and Register of Directors, must be updated to reflect the new name.

data.title: Change Company Seal and Stationery
data.description: All official stationery, including the company seal, letterheads, and business cards, must be updated with the new name.

data.title: Update Company Website and Branding
data.description: The company's digital presence, including the website, social media profiles, and branding, must be updated to reflect the new name.

data.title: Notify Stakeholders
data.description: Inform all stakeholders, including employees, customers, suppliers, and business partners, about the name change.

data.title: Tax Authorities and Regulatory Bodies
data.description: Notify relevant tax authorities, government departments, and regulatory bodies including GST authorities about the name change.

data.title: Bank Accounts
data.description: Notify the company's banks and financial institutions of the name change and update bank accounts and other financial instruments.

data.title: Update Trademarks and Intellectual Property
data.description: If applicable, ensure that any registered trademarks or intellectual property are updated to reflect the new company name.

data.description: The process involves submitting an application to the Registrar of Companies with the proposed new name, passing board and shareholder resolutions, filing Form MGT-14 and Form INC-24, and receiving a new Certificate of Incorporation.

Cancellation of GST registration can be initiated voluntarily by the registered person or mandated by tax authorities. data.title: What is GST cancellation?
data.description: GST cancellation refers to the process of terminating a GST registration for a business or individual. This can be done voluntarily by the registered person or may be initiated by tax authorities under certain conditions.

data.title: Who can apply for GST cancellation?
data.description: Any registered person or business entity can apply for GST cancellation. This includes businesses that are ceasing operations, undergoing restructuring, or those that are no longer required to be registered under GST.

data.title: What are the common reasons for GST cancellation?
data.description: Common reasons include the closure of business operations, a merger or demerger of businesses, non-compliance with GST regulations, or if the business's turnover falls below the GST registration threshold.

data.title: How can I apply for GST cancellation?
data.description: You can apply for GST cancellation online through the GST portal by navigating to the 'Services' tab, selecting 'Registration,' and clicking on 'Application for Cancellation of Registration.'

data.title: How long does the GST cancellation process take?
data.description: The GST cancellation process can take a few weeks depending on the completeness of your application and the responsiveness of the GST authorities. Typically, the authorities review and process the application within 30 days.

data.title: What should I do after my GST registration is cancelled?
data.description: After cancellation, you need to file a final GST return, ensure all tax liabilities are settled, maintain records of all business transactions, and update or close any GST-related accounts with banks.

data.title: Can I reapply for GST registration after cancellation?
data.description: Yes, you can reapply for GST registration if your business circumstances change or if you meet the eligibility criteria for GST registration. You will need to go through the standard registration process again.

data.title: What happens if I do not apply for GST cancellation but cease business operations?
data.description: Failing to apply for GST cancellation while ceasing operations can lead to penalties and interest for non-compliance, as well as ongoing obligations to file GST returns. It is important to formally cancel your GST registration to avoid such issues.

title: Income Tax Return Filing
description: Income Tax Return (ITR) filing is the process of reporting your income, deductions, taxes paid, and other financial information to the Income Tax Department of India for a particular financial year. RegistrationSeva.com offers professional ITR filing services across India, ensuring accurate tax computation, maximum eligible benefits, and timely compliance.

data.description: Income Tax Return (ITR) filing is one of the most important tax compliance requirements for individuals, businesses, professionals, LLPs, and companies. It enables taxpayers to declare their earnings, claim eligible deductions and exemptions, report capital gains, carry forward losses, and claim refunds of excess taxes paid. Apart from being a statutory obligation, an Income Tax Return serves as an important financial document for obtaining loans, applying for visas, participating in government tenders, purchasing insurance policies, and establishing income proof.

data.title: Due Dates for ITR Filing (AY 2026-27)
data.description: Individuals, HUFs and non-audit cases: 15 September 2026. Businesses requiring tax audit: 31 October 2026. Taxpayers covered under transfer pricing: 30 November 2026. The above due dates are subject to change through government notifications.

eligibility.name: Who Should File
eligibility.heading: The following individuals and entities are generally required to file an Income Tax Return in India

data.title: Individuals
data.description: Individuals whose total income exceeds the basic exemption limit, salaried employees earning taxable income, pensioners, individuals having income from house property, capital gains, interest, dividends, or other sources, and individuals who wish to claim a refund of excess TDS.

data.title: Business Owners and Professionals
data.description: Proprietorship businesses, freelancers and consultants, professionals such as doctors, architects, lawyers, engineers, and chartered accountants, and individuals opting for presumptive taxation schemes under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE.

data.title: Companies, LLPs and Firms
data.description: Private Limited Companies, Public Limited Companies, One Person Companies (OPCs), Partnership Firms, and Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs).

data.title: Other Persons Required to File ITR
data.description: Resident individuals holding foreign assets or foreign bank accounts, individuals earning foreign income, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) having taxable income in India, taxpayers seeking to carry forward losses, and persons undertaking specified high-value financial transactions.

benefits.name: Benefits
benefits.heading: Filing an Income Tax Return offers several financial, legal, and compliance-related advantages

data.title: Compliance with Tax Laws
data.description: Timely filing ensures compliance with the Income Tax Act and helps avoid penalties, interest, notices, and legal complications.

data.title: Easy Loan Approval
data.description: Banks and financial institutions often require Income Tax Returns while approving home loans, personal loans, education loans, vehicle loans, and business loans.

data.title: Claim Income Tax Refund
data.description: Taxpayers can claim refunds of excess taxes deducted through TDS, TCS, or advance tax payments.

data.title: Carry Forward of Losses
data.description: Business losses, capital losses, and certain other losses can be carried forward and adjusted against future income, subject to compliance with filing requirements.

data.title: Visa and Immigration Benefits
data.description: Most embassies and consulates require ITR acknowledgements as proof of financial stability during visa processing.

data.title: Proof of Income
data.description: An Income Tax Return acts as an authentic proof of income and financial credibility for various personal and business transactions.

data.title: Easier Business Growth

data.title: What is an Income Tax Return (ITR)?
data.description: An Income Tax Return (ITR) is a form used to report your income, deductions, taxes paid, and tax liability to the Income Tax Department of India for a particular financial year.

data.title: Who is required to file an Income Tax Return?
data.description: Individuals, professionals, businesses, LLPs, companies, and other taxpayers whose income exceeds the prescribed exemption limit or who meet specified filing conditions are required to file an ITR.

data.title: What is the due date for filing ITR for AY 2026-27?
data.description: For most individual taxpayers and non-audit cases, the due date for filing Income Tax Return for AY 2026-27 is 15 September 2026. Due dates for audit and transfer pricing cases are different.

data.title: What happens if I do not file my Income Tax Return on time?
data.description: Late filing may result in penalties, interest on outstanding taxes, delayed refunds, and restrictions on carrying forward certain losses under the Income Tax Act.

data.title: Can I file an Income Tax Return if my income is below the taxable limit?
data.description: Yes. Voluntary filing of ITR is allowed and can be beneficial for claiming tax refunds, obtaining loans, visa applications, and maintaining financial records.

data.title: Can I revise my Income Tax Return after filing?
data.description: Yes. If you discover any mistake or omission after filing your return, you can file a revised return within the time limit prescribed under the Income Tax Act.

data.title: What is Form 26AS and why is it important?
data.description: Form 26AS is a consolidated tax statement that reflects TDS, TCS, advance tax, and other tax-related transactions. It helps taxpayers verify taxes credited against their PAN before filing ITR.

data.title: How can I claim an Income Tax refund?
data.description: If excess tax has been deducted or paid during the financial year, you can claim a refund by filing your Income Tax Return. The refund is credited directly to your validated bank account after processing.

data.description: A Trademark Hearing is an important stage in the trademark registration process where the applicant is given an opportunity to present arguments and evidence before the Trademark Registrar regarding objections raised in the Examination Report. Trademark hearings are generally scheduled when the Registrar is not satisfied with the written response filed against the trademark objection or when further clarification is required before granting registration.

The purpose of a trademark hearing is to determine whether the trademark is eligible for registration under the provisions of the Trade Marks Act, 1999. During the hearing, the applicant or their authorized trademark attorney presents legal arguments, supporting documents, precedents, and evidence to establish the distinctiveness and registrability of the trademark. A successful trademark hearing can lead to the acceptance and advertisement of the trademark in the Trademark Journal.

data.title: What is a Trademark Hearing?
data.description: A Trademark Hearing is a legal proceeding conducted by the Trademark Registry to allow applicants to address objections raised against their trademark application.

data.title: Why is a Trademark Hearing scheduled?
data.description: A hearing is generally scheduled when the Registrar requires further clarification regarding objections raised in the Examination Report.

data.title: Is attendance at a Trademark Hearing mandatory?
data.description: Yes. Failure to attend the hearing may result in abandonment of the trademark application.

data.title: Can I attend the hearing personally?
data.description: Yes. Applicants may appear personally or authorize a trademark attorney or agent to represent them.

data.title: Can trademark objections be resolved during the hearing?
data.description: Yes. Many trademark objections are successfully resolved through proper legal arguments and supporting evidence presented during the hearing.

data.title: What documents are required for a Trademark Hearing?
data.description: Documents may include the hearing notice, examination report, trademark application details, invoices, advertisements, affidavits, and proof of trademark usage.

data.title: What happens after a successful Trademark Hearing?
data.description: If the Registrar is satisfied, the trademark application may be accepted and advertised in the Trademark Journal.

data.title: What happens if the Registrar is not satisfied?
data.description: The application may be refused, although legal remedies such as review or appeal may be available depending on the circumstances.
